title: Chrome-style pinned tabs: a pinned tab moves first in its pane, and Close Other Tabs keeps it
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab with the keyboard
converted from scripts/cmux-next/pinned-items-e2e.py, which stays; tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/_scripts-095.json links them

steps.note: the pinned-tab leg of scripts/cmux-next/pinned-items-e2e.py (kept), in the launch workspace: tabs t1 (the launch's), t2 and t3
the script's newSurface: a second terminal tab in the focused pane; created/0 is its public tab id
script row 'a pinned tab moves first' (the script's CLI-origin pin of t3)
script row 'Close Other Tabs keeps the pinned tab': from t2's menu, t1 closes and t3 stays

invariants: at three-tabs the launch workspace's pane lists t1, t2 and t3, none pinned
at pinned-first the pane's first tab is t3 (the id t3 created) with pinned true, followed by t1 and t2 unpinned
at kept the pane lists exactly t3 (pinned) and t2: Close Other Tabs closed only the unpinned tab it did not keep
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
ids stay stable unless the step created or closed them (I2)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: workspace tiles, top rows, Home out of and back into the top rows and their menu titles (Pin / Unpin Workspace): debug.sidebar_rows and debug.menu_item only, and the sidebar facet has no provider yet (p15-oracle-036)

the user's pins and Home edits undone by Cmd-Z after a palette run: the palette runs are keys typed into the palette panel, which debug.key reaches only with target palette, and the result is again the sidebar facet's

the script's 'Cmd-W keeps a pinned tab' row: since tabs.cmdWClosesPinnedTabs (default on) the user's Cmd-W closes a pinned tab as Chrome's does (TabLifecycle.close), so that row of the script is stale
everything across an app restart and a full restart: driver_app has no restart step (p15-oracle-023, p15-oracle-188)
